item.title: 5 Microsoft 365 Misconfigurations Exposing South African SMEs to Business Email Compromise
item.description: Business Email Compromise (BEC) rarely requires sophisticated zero-day exploits. In most incidents we investigate across South African SMEs, attackers gain access through stolen credentials and quietly abuse native Microsoft 365 features to monitor invoices, intercept payments, and exfiltrate sensitive client data—triggering mandatory breach notifications under POPIA Section 22.

item.title: POPIA Compliance for South African SMEs
item.description:
Navigating POPIA Compliance for South African SMEs in 2026

South Africa’s Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) protects personal data, forcing SMEs to handle customer, employee, and supplier info responsibly. item.title: Zero Trust Architecture
item.description:
How Zero Trust Changes Perimeter-Based Security

Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) is an approach to designing security controls, not a single product. NIST SP 800-207 describes an architecture that does not grant implicit trust based on a user’s or device’s network location or ownership. Access to an enterprise resource is authenticated and authorized before a session is established.

item.title: Automation & Tools
item.description:
Manual work is a security problem

Every hour your team spends copying alerts into a spreadsheet is an hour not spent investigating one. Toil spreads because each workaround is small and individually reasonable — until the process lives in one person’s head, at the end of a long week.

item.title: Cybersecurity R&D
item.description:
Some questions do not have an answer yet

Most security work assumes the question is known: does this control exist, does that password policy hold, can this attack succeed. Research begins where those assumptions run out — a new AI feature, an unfamiliar industrial protocol, an identity model nobody has measured yet.

item.title: Managed Cybersecurity
item.description:
Where security usually breaks down

Most South African organisations do not end up breached because they bought the wrong firewall. They end up breached because nobody is watching the alerts after hours, and the estate has quietly drifted from the configuration it was built with.

item.title: Security Training
item.description:
Most security training is forgotten by Monday

An annual slide deck and a quiz does not change what someone does when an invoice arrives with changed banking details. People fall for the same handful of attacks because the training was something they watched, not something they practised.
